plain_english_policy: HB230 (2011) is a targeted tax incentive bill designed to stimulate job creation among small businesses in Alabama. It establishes an income tax credit for employers who hire new full-time workers earning over $10/hour, with conditions tied to net employment growth and eligibility rules. The policy direction reflects a pro-business approach to economic development, prioritizing incentives for private-sector hiring while excluding larger firms (those with >50 employees) and focusing on retention of newly hired workers.

evidence_quotes: An Alabama income and financial institution excise tax credit is hereby established for small businesses that create new jobs paying more than ten dollars ($10) per hour. The credit shall equal one thousand dollars ($1,000)...
The employer must have a net increase in the total number of full-time employees... over the number employed as of the last day of the tax year immediately preceding...
This act may be cited as the 'Full Employment Act of 2011.'
